title: Brightway Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff

SE to run latency/cost benchmark on a representative prompt set; CSM to schedule weekly check-ins.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-02-08 11:00 PST / 19:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Eli Navarro (Redwood CSM), Alex Chen (Brightway CTO), Maya Ruiz (Brightway Head of ML), Sam Ortega (Brightway DevOps), Priya Patel (Brightway Product)

Summary (auto): Quick onboarding kickoff to align on pilot scope, security, and benchmarks.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you all making time. This is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Quick intros?
[00:12] Alex: Alex here, CTO at Brightway, Maya our ML lead, Sam our DevOps, Priya on product.
[00:20] Jordan: Awesome. Priya M. from our SE team will do the technical walk and then Eli our CSM to coordinate timelines.
[00:28] Priya (SE): hi all, yeah, the plan for today is to go through your stack, security reqs, pick pilot success criteria and then outline the first benchmarks. I'll also flag any potential blockers.
[00:40] Maya: sounds good. we are mainly trying to replace some of our internal LLM pipeline for summarization and triage, want to keep latency under ~250 ms for the critical path, and cost per 1k tokens ideally under $2-3 equivalent.
[01:00] Priya (SE): okay got it, low latency + cost constraints. quick question on data residency and retention, are you okay with hosted or do you require VPC/private?
[01:12] Alex: security is important \u0014 we're SOC2 in progress and will probably require KMS integration and SSO. For pilot we can start with hosted if logs and retention controls are agreed, but long term we may need a VPC/private deployment.
[01:30] Sam: also, we run everything in AWS, EKS with terraform, we prefer minimal network changes but can open peering if needed. KMS keys are on our side.
[01:42] Priya (SE): makes sense. Redwood supports hosted with customer-managed KMS via bring-your-own-key, and private deploy (VPC) for enterprise. There may be slight perf benefits on Dedicated but we can optimize. Also we use prefix/KV cache and batching to hit latency SLOs, but the effective latency depends on prompt length and concurrency.
[02:10] Maya: can you share numbers? for our 800-token average prompt what's realistic?
[02:18] Priya (SE): rough ballpark: on Hosted with our optimized kernels and quantization we often see 200-300ms for 512 tokens on x1 throughput configs, for 800 tokens it will be higher \u0014 we'll run a benchmark with your prompt set. if you need <250ms consistently we might look at Dedicated GPUs or model variant that trades a bit of quality for speed.
[02:40] Alex: how about cost tradeoffs? we don't want to overcommit to Dedicated without clear ROI.
[02:46] Jordan: totally, the pilot is the right place to determine cost/latency tradeoffs. we'll produce a benchmark sheet that shows latency and cost per 1k tokens across Hosted vs Dedicated vs small quantized variant.
[03:00] Maya: ok great. On compliance: we need audit logs, RBAC, SSO integration (SAML/Okta), and encryption at rest with our KMS. Any surprises there?
[03:12] Eli (CSM): We'll send our SOC2 summary and the security questionnaire after the call; Jordan will attach the more detailed docs. On SSO we have SAML support and role mapping for RBAC. Audit logs are available and can be exported to your SIEM.
[03:30] Sam: With private deployment, are we responsible for upgrades? we'd like automated patching if possible.
[03:36] Priya (SE): For Redwood Private we provide the control plane and the deployment packages; you manage the infra but we support automated updates through our ops tooling. We'll document the upgrade path. Note: on-prem air-gapped is a separate engagement.
[03:58] Maya: timeline wise, we want pilot results in 3 weeks, then decision to roll to production within 8 weeks. Is that feasible?
[04:08] Jordan: yes that sounds doable. Pilot in 2-3 weeks, we can parallelize security review and benchmarks. If Private is needed we'll add extra time for networking.
[04:20] Priya (SE): I'll need the sample prompt set and 3 representative payloads. Also tell us your concurrency targets (qps) and p99 latency target.
[04:30] Maya: concurrency target is 20 qps for the triage path, p99 under 500 ms and p50 under 250 ms ideally.
[04:38] Priya (SE): good. We'll run continuous batch-aware benchmarks and include KV cache effects. One note on transcriptions \u0014 our benchmark will include both cold and warm KV cache runs.
[04:52] Alex: what models are you planning to use? we care about hallucinations for clinical snippets.
[04:58] Priya (SE): we'll start with a vetted open model from our catalog, and a quantized variant as fallback. We'll also run evals tied to your prompt set to measure quality regression. If hallucination is a concern we'll tune generation parameters and possibly use reranking.
[05:12] Sam: any integration work for the SDK? we use python and Node for our backend.
[05:18] Jordan: we have SDKs for python/node/rest. For high throughput we recommend the streaming API and a batching client. We'll share code samples.
[05:30] Maya: ok, can you outline the pilot success criteria right now?
[05:34] Priya (SE): Sure: 1) p50 latency <250 ms for triage path on representative prompts, 2) p99 <500 ms at 20 qps, 3) cost per 1k tokens within agreed budget (target $2-3), 4) security checklist items validated (SOC2 doc, SSO, KMS), 5) quality metrics (ROUGE/F1 thresholds) pass on your eval set.
[06:00] Alex: that's clear. Any blockers you anticipate?
[06:04] Priya (SE): potential blockers: delayed sample data, network peering for VPC, or if the prompt lengths push latency beyond thresholds without Dedicated. We'll call these out in the benchmark report.
[06:18] Jordan: next steps recap: Jordan to share security docs and deck, Priya to run benchmarks once you share prompts, Eli to schedule weekly syncs. We'll aim to reconvene after benchmarks.
[06:32] Maya: okay thanks everyone. We'll get the prompts over by end of Friday.
[06:36] Priya (SE): quick note \u0014 we've had some transcription issues in past exports, so ignore any weird product names you see, like "Redwood Dedicate" or "KV cash" in earlier notes.
[06:48] Jordan: haha fair. Any final Qs?
[06:50] Alex: none, thanks.
[06:52] Eli (CSM): I'll send a calendar invite for weekly check-ins and the security packet after this call.
[06:58] Jordan: great, thanks all.
